subject: psychology
promptStrong: Give me a challenging GCSE exam-style question on situational and dispositional factors affecting obedience, then mark my answer against the OCR spec.
promptWeak: Explain the difference between situational and dispositional factors in social influence for GCSE OCR Psychology simply, with an example and the most common mistake.

questions.q: Conformity in the OCR spec is mainly explained through:
questions.explain: The spec explains conformity through majority influence, where the views of the larger group shape an individual's behaviour.

questions.q: A student privately disagrees but publicly agrees with the group's clearly wrong answer so as not to stand out. This is best described as:
questions.explain: Going along with the majority to fit in, despite private doubt, is conformity through majority influence.

questions.q: Obedience in the OCR spec refers to:
options: Losing your identity in a crowd
Following the orders of an authority figure
questions.explain: Obedience is following the direct orders of an authority figure, distinct from conforming to a peer majority.

questions.q: Which situational factor does the spec link to increased obedience?
options: The presence of an authority figure
questions.explain: The presence of a legitimate authority figure is a situational factor that increases obedience.

questions.q: 'Collective and crowd behaviour' in the spec includes which pair of behaviours?
questions.explain: The spec studies collective and crowd behaviour, including both pro-social and anti-social behaviour.

questions.q: Behaviour that benefits others or society, such as helping in an emergency, is called:
questions.explain: Pro-social behaviour is action that benefits others or society; anti-social behaviour is the opposite.

questions.q: Which situational factor does the spec link to pro-social and anti-social behaviour?
questions.explain: The spec identifies culture as a situational factor influencing whether behaviour is pro-social or anti-social.

questions.q: Situational factors in the OCR spec are explanations based on:
options: The influence of other people and the social setting
questions.explain: Situational factors explain behaviour through the social situation and other people, rather than the individual's personality.

questions.q: A criticism of situational explanations highlighted in the spec relates to which debate?
questions.explain: Situational explanations are criticised via the free will/determinism debate, as they suggest the situation determines behaviour.

questions.q: When people in a large crowd lose their sense of individual identity and personal responsibility, this is called:
questions.explain: Deindividuation is the loss of individual identity in a crowd, a situational factor linked to collective and crowd behaviour.

questions.q: An individual who normally behaves calmly joins a large anonymous crowd and acts aggressively. This is best explained by:
questions.explain: Losing personal identity and restraint in an anonymous crowd is deindividuation, increasing anti-social crowd behaviour.

questions.q: Dispositional factors in the spec explain behaviour through:
questions.explain: Dispositional factors are internal, explaining behaviour through the individual's personality rather than the situation.

questions.q: According to the spec, which dispositional factor is linked to conformity?
questions.explain: Self-esteem is a dispositional (personality) factor linked to conformity; people with lower self-esteem may conform more.

questions.q: In the spec, which dispositional factor is linked to behaviour in crowds?
questions.explain: Locus of control is the dispositional factor the spec links to how individuals behave within crowds.

questions.q: The dispositional factor the spec links to obedience is the:
questions.explain: The authoritarian personality is the dispositional factor associated with higher levels of obedience to authority.

questions.q: The spec links which brain region to morality as a dispositional influence on behaviour?
questions.explain: The spec links regions of the pre-frontal cortex to morality (and hippocampal volume to self-esteem) as brain influences on behaviour.

questions.q: The OCR application for Social Influence uses minority and majority influence to change attitudes towards:
questions.explain: The application focuses on how social influence can change attitudes and reduce mental health stigma and discrimination.

questions.q: The OCR core study Bickman (1974) investigated obedience by testing the effect of:
questions.explain: Bickman (1974) studied 'the social power of a uniform', finding people obeyed a guard-uniformed confederate more than one in ordinary clothes.

questions.q: Bickman's (1974) findings best support which explanation of obedience?
options: A situational factor (authority signalled by uniform)
questions.explain: Because obedience rose when the confederate wore a uniform, Bickman supports a situational explanation: the uniform signals authority.

questions.q: The OCR core study NatCen (2011) examined the involvement of young people in which real UK event?
questions.explain: The NatCen (2011) study explored why young people became involved in the August 2011 riots in England, illustrating anti-social collective behaviour and dispositional factors.

specSource: OCR GCSE (9–1) Psychology (J203) specification; Social Influence
